ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Radiation without a direct nuclear hit

Two cell cultures receive the same ionizing radiation dose. A radical scavenger decreases DNA strand damage in one culture even though radiation delivery is unchanged. Which indirect event most plausibly explains the protection?

  1. Interception of radicals generated by water radiolysis
  2. Preventing all photon entry into the cell
  3. Increasing chromosome number
  4. Blocking immunoglobulin secretion
  5. Accelerating calcium phosphate deposition
Answer and explanation

Interception of radicals generated by water radiolysis

Ionizing radiation can split water and generate radicals that subsequently injure DNA and other molecules; scavenging reduces this indirect component.

Option explanations

Interception of radicals generated by water radiolysis: Ionizing radiation can split water and generate radicals that subsequently injure DNA and other molecules; scavenging reduces this indirect component.

Preventing all photon entry into the cell: A radical scavenger does not physically shield cells from radiation.

Increasing chromosome number: Ploidy change is not the protective mechanism described.

Blocking immunoglobulin secretion: Antibody secretion does not account for acute radiation-induced DNA injury.

Accelerating calcium phosphate deposition: Calcification does not protect by intercepting aqueous radicals.
